title: Opportunity Hunter Review
prompt: Work on ilya-wizard/studyrepo using the current master branch. Read README.md, CURRENT_STATE.md, config/profile.json, config/cycle.json, config/scoring.json, the canonical data/opportunities.jsonl, data/feedback.jsonl, data/observations.jsonl, data/runs.jsonl and data/experiments before deciding. Follow the current repository protocols; the repository is the source of truth. Historical reports and scores are not current rankings. Follow prompts/review.md and prompts/validate.md. First check data consistency, source verification, user feedback and actual experiment results. Review the current cycle's two audiences, up to three opportunities and at most one active experiment. Measure independent behavioral evidence, actual user interest, real conversations, repeat use, paid commitments and spend; planned actions do not count. Separate weak solutions from strong underlying problems. If no test is active, finish preparation of the strongest option and request a user choice only if not already requested. If an experiment is active, summarize what happened and choose continue/change/watch/reject using its predefined thresholds. Update cycle dates and focus when needed, preserving the configured recurring cadence. Save a short weekly review artifact even when no notification is warranted. Notify for changed evidence, a genuine decision, an experiment milestone or a new actionable blocker; do not repeatedly notify unchanged uncertainty. Persist actual evidence, decisions and progress with stable IDs; validate schemas/provenance/budget, regenerate CURRENT_STATE and compatibility views, and commit coherent changes against the latest remote head without force-pushing. Log actual queries, sources, changes, blockers and notification event keys, even if no new candidate. Do not invent ratings, contacts, interviews, payments or completed tests. Do not send messages, spend money or use someone else's voice/content unless explicitly authorized for that action. Keep participant information redacted because this repository is public. If GitHub access or validation fails, say so; never claim saved or tested work that did not succeed. User-facing updates should be concise Russian, with concrete evidence and the next decision; avoid jargon and repeated unchanged notifications.
